relationship.rule: A production capability is not release-complete until its learning entry exists and passes the learning sync gate.

project_journey.title: Separate app stacks
project_journey.problem: Each app could accumulate its own models, packages and recovery logic.
project_journey.change: Identify reusable local services instead of duplicating them.
project_journey.result: The need for a shared foundation became explicit.

project_journey.title: Forge Base
project_journey.problem: A missing executable or hosted helper could stop a workflow.
project_journey.change: Add Doctor checks, fallback routing, caches and offline recovery rules.
project_journey.result: Failures became routable instead of terminal.

project_journey.title: Forge Core
project_journey.problem: Elias, MedForge and GrimForge still needed a common runtime contract.
project_journey.change: Expose reasoning, search, vision, speech, transcription, diagrams, video and provenance through one local API.
project_journey.result: One backend can serve multiple working apps.

project_journey.title: Forge Bridge
project_journey.problem: Hosted HTTPS apps cannot always call local HTTP safely.
project_journey.change: Add loopback SDK support plus export/import fallback rather than weakening browser security.
project_journey.result: Hosted UIs can remain optional companions to the local node.

project_journey.title: Vault + provenance
project_journey.problem: Evidence work needs preserved originals and source-linked claims.
project_journey.change: Add SHA-256 storage, SQLite metadata, local search and provenance-aware outputs.
project_journey.result: Elias can reason from retained sources instead of loose uploads.

project_journey.title: Shared app integrations
project_journey.problem: The backend only pays off when real apps actually depend on it.
project_journey.change: Connect Elias, MedForge and GrimForge to standard Forge endpoints and local fallbacks.
project_journey.result: The production apps share infrastructure instead of cloning it.

project_journey.title: Workspace / Learn split
project_journey.problem: The teaching UI and working UI were becoming one confusing product.
project_journey.change: Keep Forge Workspace production-focused and move lessons, history, glossary, simulation and testing into Forge Learn.
project_journey.result: Two sibling products stay synchronized through one learning manifest and release gate.

project_journey.title: UI/UX restoration
project_journey.problem: The Workspace/Learn split accidentally replaced mature product surfaces with thin diagnostic pages.
project_journey.change: Keep the split architecture but restore rich working interfaces for Workspace, Elias, MedForge and GrimForge, exposing the existing Core capabilities instead of hiding them.
project_journey.result: Teaching stays separate without sacrificing the production experience.

project_journey.title: Product polish and real workflow parity
project_journey.problem: The apps shared a strong Core but still looked and behaved like uneven prototypes.
project_journey.change: Added a premium six-product design system, primary-action hierarchy, richer progress states, deeper app Copilots, and explicit GrimForge animation modes.
project_journey.result: The suite can evolve its backend without sacrificing product identity or hiding what a workflow actually does.

project_journey.title: Workflow regression recovery
project_journey.problem: Product-polish wiring exposed advanced controls but allowed one-click workflows to dead-end or regress to thinner outputs.
project_journey.change: Added renderer preflight/fallback routing, restored a full MedForge teaching-package workflow, and upgraded Evidence Auditor to source-controlled defense-style PDFs with intact exhibits.
project_journey.result: The visible primary action is again tied to an end-to-end working workflow, with fallbacks disclosed rather than silently failing or substituting evidence.

frontend.definition: The part of an app a person sees and clicks.
frontend.forge_example: The Elias, MedForge and GrimForge local pages are frontends.

backend.definition: The hidden services that perform the work.
backend.forge_example: Forge Core is the shared backend.

API.definition: A defined way for software to ask other software to do work.
API.forge_example: Elias calls Forge endpoints for evidence search.

endpoint.definition: One specific API address for one kind of action.

JSON.definition: Structured text used to exchange named values and lists.
JSON.forge_example: Forge returns job results and status as JSON.

dependency.definition: Software another piece of software needs in order to work.

fallback.definition: The next safe route when the preferred route is unavailable.
fallback.forge_example: llama.cpp can follow Ollama in the reasoning chain.

SDK.definition: Helper code that makes an API easier for another app to use.
SDK.forge_example: Forge ships TypeScript and Python SDKs.

localhost.definition: Your own computer acting as a server.

database.definition: Persistent structured storage that can be queried later.

schema.definition: Rules describing the fields and shape data should follow.
schema.forge_example: The learning manifest itself has a schema version.

provenance.definition: A record of where information or an output came from.
provenance.forge_example: Evidence claims keep links to their retained sources.

2.5D.definition: A 2D image is animated with camera/depth-style motion so it feels spatial without becoming a full 3D scene.
2.5D.forge_example: GrimForge generates an illustrated shot, then FFmpeg adds controlled cinematic depth motion.

Render pipeline.definition: The ordered stages that turn source material into a finished media file.
Render pipeline.forge_example: GrimForge: script → images/sets → animation → voice → captions → final MP4.

Visual regression.definition: Checking that a new build still matches an approved design instead of slowly drifting or losing UI features.
Visual regression.forge_example: Forge v0.5.5 treats the six-app showcase and GrimForge Simple concept as design acceptance references.

lesson.title: How MedForge Full Teaching Package works
lesson.summary: How one MedForge action runs image inspection, mechanism teaching, illustration when available, Blender 3D, and a teaching PDF.
lesson.why_it_exists: MedForge should feel like one medical-visual studio rather than disconnected utilities.
walkthrough: Start from the primary action in the working app.
Run the preflight/source-control checks before expensive work begins.
Follow each stage through Forge Core and watch how optional engines are handled.
Inspect the produced artifact and its manifest/provenance boundary.
Compare the exact route used with the route the user originally selected.

build_story.text: A polished interface existed, but the end-to-end workflow could still stop or produce a thinner artifact.
The primary button was redefined as a complete workflow rather than a collection of disconnected controls.
Forge now uses explicit fallback or source-control rules instead of silently substituting evidence or media.
Fixture tests verify the artifact exists and retains the required provenance or render-route information.
Forge Learn documents the recovery so later UI changes cannot repeat the regression.

features.tester_check: Run the package with ComfyUI offline and confirm it still produces a PDF; on Windows with Blender installed confirm still, MP4 and .blend are also produced.
